items.question: Under what condition must concealment be carried out in the mortal world among the lowest of men?
premises: Concealment is something that must be done.
Effort is the means for such concealment.
This duty applies in the mortal world among the lowest of men.
items.inference: Concealment requires deliberate effort in the setting of the mortal world among the lowest of men.
items.plain_english: What is to be concealed must be concealed with effort in the mortal world, among the lowest of men.

items.question: What qualification must hold for something previously accomplished to be fit for giving after a year of testing?
premises: Something is to be given.
That thing belongs to what was previously accomplished.
It must have been tested for one year to qualify.
items.inference: Only what was previously accomplished and tested for one year is fit to be given.
items.plain_english: What was previously accomplished and tested for one year is to be given.

items.question: By what origin is the fifth chapter identified in this sequence?
premises: A chapter is under consideration.
That chapter emerged from Candradvīpa.
It stands as the fifth in order.
items.inference: The fifth chapter is the one that emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: The fifth chapter is the one that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By what means does the speaker come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of the Kaulas.
The speaker has come to know something.
That knowledge comes by the grace of the addressee.
What is known is the determination of the Kaula teaching.
items.inference: By the grace of the lord of the Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.
items.plain_english: By your grace, O lord of the Kaulas, I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What two points of inquiry arise regarding the soul: its identity when declared, and its own nature?
premises: A soul is said to be declared.
It is asked who that soul is.
It is asked what the nature of the soul is.
items.inference: The inquiry concerns both the identity of the declared soul and the nature of the soul itself.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that is declared? Or what is the nature of the soul?

rows.grounds: interrogative pronoun with fused sandhi as given

items.question: In what context is it asked that all of what dissolves be told, specifying where dissolution occurs?
premises: Dissolution is said to occur in some place.
All that undergoes dissolution is under consideration.
The speaker asks to be told all of that.
items.inference: The inquiry seeks to know the locus of dissolution and to have all related matters told.
items.plain_english: And indeed, in what does it go to dissolution? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What set of attributes is affirmed of that which is identified as the supreme reality?
premises: A single entity is under consideration.
That entity is supreme.
That entity is partless, eternal, free from flaw, and stainless.
items.inference: That entity is affirmed as supreme, partless, eternal, free from flaw, and stainless.
items.plain_english: He is the supreme, partless, eternal one, free from flaw and stainless.

rows.grounds: nominative of paratara with sandhi as given

items.question: What identity is established for the soul that is more supreme, identified as Haṃsa and as power-individual?
premises: The soul is more supreme.
That which is more supreme is the one called Haṃsa.
That same one is called power-individual.
items.inference: The more supreme soul is identified as Haṃsa and as power-individual.
items.plain_english: He is the soul, more supreme. Indeed, he is Haṃsa, the power-individual.

rows.grounds: compound = samīra+pūraka; nominative with sandhi as given

items.question: Where is the wind-filled air affirmed to be situated?
premises: There is an air described as wind-filled.
That air is under consideration.
It is situated in all beings.
items.inference: The wind-filled air is situated in all beings.
items.plain_english: The wind-filled air is situated in all beings.

rows.grounds: demonstrative pronoun with sandhi as given
nominative of śiva with sandhi as given

items.question: Under what condition is that entity called the supreme Śiva?
premises: An entity is under consideration.
The condition is merely leaving the body.
Upon that condition, that entity is called the supreme Śiva.
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that entity is called the supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: He, upon merely leaving the body, is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: What kind of teaching is affirmed to be heard abiding in the ear, addressed to the Goddess?
premises: Something is heard abiding in the ear.
That something has come down through tradition in order.
This is addressed to the Goddess.
items.inference: What comes down through tradition in order is heard abiding in the ear.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, what has come down through tradition in order is heard abiding in the ear.

items.question: By what means is effect affirmed to follow, addressed to the fair-faced one?
premises: An address is made to the fair-faced one.
A means is specified as mere knowledge.
That means is also specified as what has been heard.
items.inference: By mere knowledge, and by what has been heard, the result follows.
items.plain_english: By this mere knowledge, and by what has been heard, O fair-faced one.

rows.grounds: ablative of ṣaṇmāsa with sandhi as given

items.question: What practice is enjoined for one who wears an ochre robe free from bondage, and over what time span?
premises: A person wears an ochre robe free from bondage.
That person should practice.
The practice is to be undertaken from six months onward.
items.inference: One who wears an ochre robe free from bondage should practice from six months onward.
items.plain_english: Whoever wears an ochre robe free from bondage should practice from six months onward.

rows.grounds: compound = sarva+vyādhi+vinirmukta; nominative with sandhi as given

items.question: What state is attained by one freed from all diseases in relation to yogis?
premises: One is freed from all diseases.
That one is in relation to yogis.
That relation results in union together.
items.inference: One freed from all diseases attains union together with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, one attains union together with yogis.

items.question: What has been declared to the addressee regarding the practice of the soul?
premises: An address is made to Bhairavī.
Something is told to her.
That something is the practice of the soul.
items.inference: The practice of the soul has been told to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: This practice of the soul has been told to you, and to you, O Bhairavī.

items.question: To what kind of person is something to be given according to this instruction?
premises: Something is to be given.
It is to be given to one endowed with all states.
It is to be given to one of resolved mind.
items.inference: What is to be given is to be given to one endowed with all states and of resolved mind.
items.plain_english: It is to be given to one endowed with all states, to one of resolved mind.

items.question: What restriction applies to giving the Kaula essence in relation to Yoginīs and their origin?
premises: The Kaula essence is under consideration.
It is not to be given.
A restriction is noted in relation to Yoginīs and their origin.
items.inference: The Kaula essence is not to be given, particularly in relation to Yoginīs and their origin.
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence is not to be given, indeed, to Yoginīs by origin.

items.question: In what condition is the speaker's body affirmed to be today?
premises: The speaker refers to their own body.
The body is pure.
The body is struck by a veil of ignorance.
items.inference: Today the speaker's pure body is struck by a veil of ignorance.
items.plain_english: Today my pure body is struck by a veil of ignorance.

items.question: What does the speaker wish to hear now, and with what qualification?
premises: The speaker wishes to hear something now.
That something is the deception of time.
That deception is described as auspicious.
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear of the auspicious deception of time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear of the auspicious deception of time.

rows.grounds: nominative of mṛtyu with sandhi as given

items.question: What assurance is given about the destruction of death?
premises: The speaker tells something.
There is no doubt.
Death is destroyed in the manner stated.
items.inference: The speaker tells how death is destroyed, with no doubt on the matter.
items.plain_english: I tell it; there is no doubt, that death is destroyed.

rows.grounds: present passive participle of dah with sandhi as given
nominative of sudhī with sandhi as given

items.question: What condition is affirmed even for the wise one in relation to nectar and essence?
premises: Reference is made to the tip of nectar.
Reference is made to the tip of essence as a means.
Even the wise one, while burning, is under consideration.
items.inference: Even the wise one, burning with the tip of essence at the tip of nectar, remains under that condition.
uncertainties: Exact syntactic relation between the compounds remains open from the tokens alone.
items.plain_english: At the tip of nectar, with the tip of essence, even the wise one burns.

rows.grounds: verb pā optative 3.sg.active with sandhi as given

items.question: What action is enjoined at the root of the tongue and palate, and how is it to be performed?
premises: The locus is the root of the tongue and palate.
Air is to be taken there.
That air should be drunk slowly.
items.inference: Having placed air at the root of the tongue and palate, one should drink it slowly.
items.plain_english: Having placed air at the root of the tongue and palate, one should drink it slowly.

rows.grounds: compound = yadā+abhyasta; nominative with sandhi as given
compound = jarā+mṛtyu; nominative with sandhi as given

items.question: Under what temporal condition are old age and death destroyed?
premises: Practice is undertaken for one year.
When that practice has been done, a condition holds.
Old age and death are destroyed under that condition.
items.inference: When the practice has been undertaken for one year, old age and death are destroyed.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

rows.grounds: past passive participle of daṃś with sandhi as given

items.question: What is affirmed about poison entering the body even in the case of a bite from great serpents?
premises: A person may be bitten by great serpents.
Poison is under consideration.
Poison does not enter the body in that case.
items.inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if bitten by great serpents.
